title: Microfluidic Fabrication of Polymeric and Biohybrid Fibers with Predesigned Size and Shape
protocol: Design and simulate the microchannel using computational fluid dynamics software (COMSOL).
Create a computer model of the desired microchannel to be imported into the simulation software.
Calculate the fluid velocity and convection/diffusion within the microchannel accurately.
Assign proper viscosity values for each incoming fluid in the simulation.
Assemble the microchannel device from aluminum and plastic parts fabricated by CNC milling and PDMS casting.
Control flow through the microchannel using three syringe pumps.
Import the designed microchannel into COMSOL.
Initialize program settings and choose 3D Laminar Flow+Convection/Diffusion Equations.
Design a finite-element mesh with small divisions at areas where properties change rapidly, especially at the shaping feature and exit to less than 1 μm side-length.
Input material properties for fluid flow, including viscosity, diffusion constant, and concentration.
Set boundary conditions for the exit flow, using zero viscous stress to simulate an open outlet.
Calculate fluid flow velocity studies by cycling through a series of input flow rates, such as core fluid = 7.5 μl/min and sheath fluid = 30 μl/min.
Import the velocity field solutions as initial values to solve convection/diffusion properties of the microchannel flow.
From the computational results, predict the number and type of shaping features to attain the desired fiber shape.
Correlate fluid flow rate inputs to the required flow rates for generating fibers.
Fabricate a microchannel device for extrusion of polymer fibers using predictions from computational results.
Choose direct micromilling, hot-embossing, or polymer casting to create sheath flow apparatus components based on available resources.
Develop a 3D model of the system via computer aided drafting (CAD) compatible with COMSOL simulations.
Create a separate CAD file for each layer of the device.
Import CAD models into a computer aided machining application to generate NC code.
Acquire 5 sheets of sacrificial layer materials that are at least 30.5 cm × 30.5 cm and 3.2 mm thick.
Acquire 1 sheet each of COC, PEEK, aluminum, and poly(methylmethacrylate) measuring 30.5 cm × 30.5 cm and 3.2 mm thick.
Acquire 1 sheet of aluminum that measures 30.5 cm × 30.5 cm and 9.5 mm thick.
Affix each sheet from steps 2.4 to 2.6 to a sacrificial stock with double-sided adhesive, ensuring an outer un-taped border no larger than 2.5 cm.
Fasten the COC + sacrificial stock to the table of the CNC Mill.
Load the tools quoted in the numeric code (NC) into the CNC mill.
Calibrate the tools and stock materials along x, y, and z axes.
Load the NC code into the CNC mill.
Mill the COC layer using the CNC mill.
Remove the machined part from the substrate.
Rinse the part thoroughly to remove mill coolant.
Wash the part with a mild detergent.
Wash the part with 70% isopropyl alcohol.
Sonicate the part if burrs are trapped in microarchitectures.
Repeat steps for each layer used to create the sheath flow device.
Combine 10 parts Sylgard 184 base with 1 part curing agent and mix thoroughly.
Pour the Sylgard 184 into the PMMA mold cavity, ensuring air bubbles are eliminated.
Cure the PDMS at room temperature for 48 hours.
Alternatively, cure the PDMS at 100 °C for 45 minutes.
Alternatively, cure the PDMS at 125 °C for 20 minutes.
Alternatively, cure the PDMS at 150 °C for 10 minutes.
Place one fastening plate at the bottom for assembly of the sheath flow device.
Attach the COC layer followed by another COC layer on top.
Position the remaining fastening plate on top.
Align shaping grooves along the edges of the channel and fluid shaping geometries in the COC layers perfectly overlap.
Insert bolts across the center of the device.
Hand tighten nuts and bolts to clamp the device together.
Alternating from left to right, repeat tightening from the center outwards to lock in alignment and prevent leaks.
Add inlet chuck when mounting holes are reached.
Continue mounting screws alternately until assembly is complete.
Use standard HPLC fittings to interface sheath flow device with tubing and syringes containing sheath fluid and prepolymer solution.
Hand tighten all connections securely.
Mount the assembled device vertically using a ring stand and clamp.
Ensure vertical alignment of the device using a level on the top portion.
Position UV source perpendicularly about 1 cm from COC face of the sheath flow device to irradiate last 3-5 cm of microchannel.
Calibrate UV source to deliver approximately 200 mW/cm².
Prepare an aliquot of polyethylene glycol 400 (PEG 400) to serve as the sheath fluid.
Fill a 1 ml Luer-tipped syringe with PEG 400 to serve as a nonpolymerizable core fluid.
Fill a 30 ml Luer-tipped syringe with PEG 400 to serve as the sheath fluid.
Mix 0.01 mol pentaerythritol tetrakis 3-mercaptopropionate (PETMP) and 0.01 mol 1,7-octadiyne (ODY).
Supplement the PETMP/ODY solution with 4 x 10^-4 mol 2,2-dimethoxy-2-phenylacetophenone (DMPA) photoinitiator.
Load a 5 ml aluminum foil-wrapped, Luer-tipped syringe with the prepolymer solution.
Ensure that the outlet of the microfluidic channel is in contact with a solution in the collection bath.
Set the core, cladding, and sheath fluid syringe pumps to infuse at 1, 30, and 120 µl/min respectively.
Mount the syringes into their corresponding syringe pumps.
Connect the syringes to the sheath flow device with UV protective Tygon tubing.
Start the sheath fluid to prime the sheath flow device and eliminate air from the system.
Visually inspect the microchannel for air bubbles.
Agitate the device by rotating and/or tapping gently while under flow if air bubbles are present.
Ensure that no air bubbles remain in the microchannel before proceeding.
Start the cladding fluid, allowing the flow to stabilize.
Inspect the microchannel again, paying particular attention to the shaping grooves.
Agitate the device while under flow to flush out any air bubbles.
Finally, start the core fluid.
Ensure that bubbles aren’t present in the system.
Turn on the UV source.
Observe the collection bath for continuous production of the hollow microfiber as it is ejected with the sheath fluid.
Retrieve the fiber from the collection bath using a modified spatula or an inoculating loop.
Allow the continuous fiber to be collected on a motorized spool.
